+## Audio announcements for recording and transcription
+
+You can enable audio announcements to notify users when recording or transcription starts in Teams meetings and VoIP calls. Announcements help participants stay informed and improve accessibility awareness. Whether a user hears an announcement depends on that user's assigned policy, not just the meeting organizer's policy.
+
+Use the **`-RecordingAndTranscriptionAudioNotification`** parameter in [Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy](/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy#-recordingandtranscriptionaudionotification) for meetings and group calls, and in [Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy](/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamscallingpolicy#-recordingandtranscriptionaudionotification) for 1:1 VoIP calls. The default value is **Disabled**. Set it to **Enabled** to turn on announcements, or **Disabled** to turn them off.
+
+For example, to enable announcements in the global meeting and calling policies, run:
+
+```powershell
+Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Global -RecordingAndTranscriptionAudioNotification Enabled
+Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -RecordingAndTranscriptionAudioNotification Enabled
+```
+
+Changes to the global policies apply to users who don't have custom policies assigned. To enable announcements for specific users or groups instead, configure custom meeting and calling policies and [assign those policies to the users or groups](assign-policies-users-and-groups).
+
+Supported clients include Windows and macOS desktop, web, Microsoft Teams Rooms, Android, iOS, and VDI 2.0. VDI 1.0 isn't supported.
+
+Note
+
+This policy doesn't control audio announcements for PSTN users or for Teams users in 1:1 calls between Teams and PSTN. Audio announcements for these scenarios are enabled by default.
+
 ## Require participant agreement for recording
 
 With a Teams meeting policy, you can require participants to agree to being recorded before they can unmute or turn on their camera. Consent results are stored in the meeting attendance report. For details, see [Require participant agreement for recording](participant-agreement-recording-transcription).

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams Mobile: Introducing shared call history in the Queues app
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams mobile Queues app now offers shared call history for authorized representatives, showing missed, answered, outgoing, and voicemail calls. Rolling out worldwide in December 2026, it helps teams manage calls efficiently with status updates and filtering, extending desktop features to mobile without new admin actions.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

We are introducing shared call history in the Queues app on Microsoft Teams mobile, allowing authorized call queue representatives to view calls handled across their queue. This includes missed, answered, outgoing, and voicemail calls. By extending the existing desktop experience to mobile, we are helping teams coordinate customer follow-ups, avoid duplicate callbacks, and manage calls more efficiently while working away from their desks.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Representatives and supervisors with access to shared call history in the Queues app, which is included with a Teams Premium license.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams mobile, Queues app

What will happen

  • Authorized representatives can view shared call history across their call queue, including missed, answered, outgoing, and voicemail calls. Shared call history on mobile uses the same administrative settings as the desktop experience.

  • Users can filter call history by resolution status to identify calls that need attention.

  • Users can tap a call to view details, including the caller, call type, time, voicemail or forwarding information, and a timeline of the call's progression through the queue.

  • The system automatically marks missed calls as Unresolved, allowing representatives to identify customers who need follow-up.
  • Users can change missed call statuses to In progress or Resolved. All queue members with access to shared call history can see the updated status, who made the change, and when.
  • Users without shared call history enabled will continue to see only their personal call history.

Action required and recommendations

No new administrative action is required for this rollout. We recommend that you inform call queue representatives about the new mobile experience, particularly how to update missed call statuses to avoid duplicate follow-ups.

  • If your organization already uses shared call history, eligible users will automatically receive the mobile experience.
  • If shared call history is not enabled, you can enable it in the Teams admin center by creating a Shared Call History template and assigning it to your call queues. You can grant access to all queue members or restrict access to authorized users.

Learn more

  • Planning - Shared Call History for voice applications - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Audio announcement for Recording and Transcription
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams now supports an optional audio announcement when recording or transcription starts, configurable via Meeting and Calling Policies. Rolling out from May 2026 to January 2027 worldwide. No admin action required; default is off. Compliance recording is not supported with this feature.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and Why:

The recording feature in Microsoft Teams now supports an audio announcement for Teams meetings and calls. With this new functionality, admins can enable a policy that plays an audio announcement when recording or transcription starts. This can be applied tenant-wide or to specific groups. The announcement helps ensure allowed participants who are permitted by policy are informed and improves accessibility awareness. This setting is available in both Meeting Policy and Calling Policy.

Rollout Schedule:

Public Preview (Worldwide): We began rolling out on early May 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by early January 2027.

General Availability (GCC): We will begin rolling out on mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

General Availability (GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out on mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

Impact on Your Organization:

None.

Action Required/Recommendations:

No admin action is required. The default audio announcement policy is OFF; it can be turned on as needed.

Compliance considerations:

Confirmed that compliance recording is not supported with this feature. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: End of support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will end support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 starting mid-December 2026, requiring iOS/iPadOS 18 or later for new releases. Existing versions will keep working without support. Organizations should notify users, encourage OS upgrades, update policies, and revise support documentation accordingly.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and Why:

Microsoft Teams is ending support for upcoming builds on iOS 17 and iPadOS 17. As this change rolls out, new Teams releases will require iOS 18 or later on iPhone and iPadOS 18 or later on iPad.

Rollout Schedule:

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by early January 2027.

Impact on Your Organization:

Users whose devices remain on iOS 17 or iPadOS 17 will not be able to install newer Teams releases that require a newer operating system.

Teams versions already installed on these devices will continue functioning without official support. This change does not introduce a block on opening or signing in to those existing installations.

Action Required/Recommendations:

  • Identify devices running iOS 17 or iPadOS 17 and notify affected users.
  • Advise users to upgrade to a supported operating system, then update Teams through the Apple App Store, to continue receiving supported Teams releases.
  • Review any mobile device management (MDM) or app deployment policies that pin or require specific iOS/iPadOS versions, and update them to allow iOS 18/iPadOS 18 so affected devices are not blocked from upgrading.
  • Update internal support documentation and helpdesk guidance.

Learn more: Hardware requirements for Microsoft Teams.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Registration capacity for town halls and webinars increases to 20,000
messageCenterItems.summary: Starting December 2026, Microsoft Teams town halls and webinars registration capacity increases up to 20,000, scaling with attendee capacity. Teams Enterprise allows 3,000 registrations; Attendee Capacity Packs enable up to 20,000. No new policies needed; organizers should ensure proper licensing and update training accordingly.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

Starting in December, registration capacity for Microsoft Teams town halls and webinars scales with the event's attendee capacity, up to 20,000 registrations per event. Organizers with Teams Enterprise can allow up to 3,000 registrations. Organizers with Attendee Capacity Packs can allow up to 20,000. Organizers can use this to plan large-scale events with registration.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early December 2026 and expect to complete by late December 2026.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizers of Teams town halls and webinars that use registration
  • Admins who manage Teams events policies and Attendee Capacity Pack licenses

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams (town halls and webinars)

What will happen

  • Registration capacity scales with attendee capacity, up to 20,000 registrations per event.
  • Organizers with Teams Enterprise can allow up to 3,000 registrations.
  • Organizers with Attendee Capacity Packs can allow up to 20,000 registrations.
  • Large webinars with registration don't support broadcast-style streaming, which is available with town halls.
  • Organizers still need the right events policy. No new policy access is needed, only the right Attendee Capacity Pack where applicable.
  • Existing Teams events policies and admin controls don't change.
  • We plan to support more registrations per event in future releases.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required. To prepare, you can:

  • Tell organizers about the higher registration limits.
  • Make sure organizers who need more than 3,000 registrations per event have an Attendee Capacity Pack of the right size. Assign packs in the Teams admin center (Add-on Licenses > Teams Events).
  • Update internal training and documentation that mention a 1,000-registration limit.
  • Review your Teams events policies in the Teams admin center (Meetings > Events policies) to confirm they meet your organization's needs.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: External presenters can manage event production controls
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams now allows event organizers to grant trusted external presenters (federated B2B and guest users) production control during events, enabling them to manage attendee viewing. This feature, rolling out August to November 2026, requires explicit organizer assignment and supports collaboration with external partners.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 17, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Organizations can now allow trusted external presenters to manage Microsoft Teams event production controls. Federated (B2B) users and guest users can be assigned through the Who has control of production tools setting, enabling them to manage the attendee viewing experience during Teams events.

This feature helps organizations that work with external event producers, agencies, and third-party event management partners by allowing authorized external presenters to perform production tasks without requiring internal staff to manage the event.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 567298.

Rollout schedule

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in early August 2026 and expected to complete by early October 2026 (previously early September) (previously mid-August)
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning early August 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously early November)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations that use Microsoft Teams events
  • Event organizers who work with external presenters, production vendors, agencies, or trusted partners
  • Federated (B2B) users and guest users who are invited to participate in Teams events

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Teams events

What will happen

  • Event organizers can grant production control permissions to federated (B2B) users and guest users.
  • Authorized external presenters can manage production controls and determine what attendees see during an event.
  • The feature is available only when an organizer explicitly assigns production control access.
  • Existing events and configurations will not be modified automatically.

Action required and recommendations

No admin action is required before rollout.

We recommend that you:

  • Review internal guidance and governance policies for Teams events that include external participants.
  • Inform event organizers about this new capability.
  • Determine which external presenters, vendors, or partners should be authorized to receive production control permissions.
  • Update any training or documentation used by event organizers, if applicable.

Organizers can use the Who has control of production tools setting when configuring a Teams event to grant production access to trusted external users.

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does this change provide a new way for users, tenants, or subscriptions to communicate?Yes. This feature enables organizations to include federated (B2B) and guest users in Teams event production workflows, expanding collaboration and communication capabilities with trusted external participants.
Does this change include an admin or organizer control?Yes. Event organizers can use the Who has control of production tools setting to grant or restrict production control access for trusted external users when configuring a Teams event.
Can users enable or disable this capability themselves?Yes. Event organizers can choose whether to grant production control permissions to federated (B2B) and guest users when setting up an event.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams Town halls: Upload custom backgrounds in Manage what attendees see
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will allow organizers and presenters of town hall events with Teams Premium licenses to upload custom background images in the "Manage what attendees see" feature. Rollout begins early June 2026, enabling branded visuals behind presenters and shared content in supported layouts, with no admin action needed.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 17, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

Introduction

To help organizations deliver more polished and branded town hall events, Microsoft Teams is introducing the ability for organizers and presenters to upload custom background images in the Manage what attendees see experience. This enhancement allows teams to replace default backgrounds with branded visuals—such as company logos or event-specific designs—so presenters and shared content appear consistently on brand for attendees. This feature is available for Teams events organizers with a Teams Enterprise license. This update applies to Teams for Windows desktop and Mac desktop.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 561493.

When this will happen

  • Targeted Release: Rollout begins in early June 2026 (previously late May) and is expected to complete by early June 2026 (previously late May).
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in early June 2026 and is expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously early November).

How this affects your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizers and presenters of Teams town hall events
  • Users assigned a Teams Premium license
  • Tenants using Manage what attendees see in town halls

What will happen

  • Organizers and presenters can upload custom background images directly within the Manage what attendees see experience.
  • Uploaded backgrounds appear behind presenters and shared content in supported town hall layouts.
  • JPEG and PNG image formats are supported, with recommended resolution guidance shown during upload.
  • Custom backgrounds appear alongside existing default background options in the background picker.
  • The feature is enabled by default for eligible users and applies only to town hall events where Manage what attendees see is enabled.
  • There is no change to standard Teams meetings or webinars.

What you can do to prepare

  • No admin action is required before rollout.
  • Consider notifying users who organize or present town halls about this new capability.
  • Prepare branded background images that align with your organization’s visual identity guidelines.
  • Update internal documentation or event playbooks if you provide guidance on hosting town halls.
  • Optionally, run a test town hall event to familiarize presenters with the upload flow and attendee experience.

Learn more: Customize the event screen - Manage what attendees see in Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Support

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data?Yes. Uploaded custom background images are stored as part of the Teams town hall event configuration.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed or accessed?Yes. Background images are rendered behind presenters and shared content during the live event for attendees.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Report guest invitations for security concerns
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will let users report suspicious guest invitations for security concerns starting late November 2026. Reports go to IT admins via the Teams admin center. No action is needed if "Report a security concern" is already enabled in messaging policies, which control this feature.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 17, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and Why:

Microsoft Teams will enable users to report guest invitations for security concerns directly from Teams. When users receive an unexpected or potentially malicious invitation to join another organization as a guest, they can report it to their IT admin for review, helping identify and mitigate phishing and other abuse through guest invitations.

Rollout Schedule:

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late November 2026 (previously mid-November) and expect to complete by late November 2026 (previously mid-November).

Impact on Your Organization:

Users can report suspicious guest invitations when declining them in Teams. Reports are shared with their IT admin through the User reported security submissions report in the Teams admin center and with Microsoft for review.

Action Required/Recommendations:

No action is required for organizations that already have Report a security concern enabled in their Teams messaging policy. Admins can manage this capability through Teams admin center > Messaging policies > Report a security concern.

Compliance considerations:

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. The capability is controlled through the Teams messaging policy setting for Report a security concern.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Third-party synthetic audio and video detection in meetings
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will support certified third-party synthetic audio and video detection in meetings starting late November 2026. Organizations can integrate these solutions to enhance security against AI-generated media threats. Admins must deploy provider apps, grant permissions, and configure meeting policies. Detection is performed by third parties, with Microsoft Teams enabling integration.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 17, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and Why:

Organizations can enhance meeting security with synthetic audio and video detection solutions provided by certified third-party providers. Third-party detection solutions analyze meeting media for signs of synthetic or manipulated audio and video and send detection signals to Teams, enabling integrated in-meeting experiences and controls.

Important: Synthetic media detection is performed by the third-party provider. Microsoft Teams provides the platform integration and experiences for surfacing and acting on detection signals from supported providers.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 573451.

Rollout Schedule:

Targeted Release (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late November 2026 (previously mid-November) and expect to complete by late November 2026.

General Availability (Worldwide): We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

Impact on Your Organization:

Organizations can choose and integrate certified third-party deepfake detection solutions into Microsoft Teams meetings, helping protect users from emerging AI-generated voice and video threats. This gives customers more flexibility to meet security and compliance needs while enabling users to make more informed trust decisions during meetings.

Action Required/Recommendations:

To use third-party Synthetic Audio and Video Detection in Microsoft Teams, administrators should evaluate and select a supported detection provider, deploy the provider app through Manage apps in the Teams admin center, grant required permissions, and configure applicable Teams meeting policies.

Compliance considerations:

QuestionAnswer
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. Certified third-party providers may analyze meeting audio/video signals for synthetic media detection. Review provider terms, data handling, and compliance documentation before enabling.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Admins manage provider app deployment, permissions, and Teams meeting policy configuration.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Onboarding workflow for new team members
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will introduce an onboarding workflow to automatically connect new members to relevant channels, improving engagement and onboarding speed. Rollout starts late November 2026 for Targeted Release and early December 2026 for General Availability. No admin action is required.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 17, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and Why:

Microsoft Teams is introducing an onboarding workflow that helps new team members get started faster by automatically connecting them to relevant channels when they join a team. This can improve engagement, accelerate onboarding, and make important information easier to find from the start.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 573452.

Rollout Schedule:

Targeted Release (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late November 2026 (previously mid-November) and expect to complete in late November 2026 (previously mid-November).

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early December 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

Impact on Your Organization:

Today, new team members may need to manually discover and join the channels that are most relevant to their work. With this update, team owners can automatically add new members to relevant channels through the onboarding workflow when they are added to a team.

Action Required/Recommendations:

No admin action is required. You may want to inform team owners about this upcoming improvement so they understand how to connect new members to relevant channels more efficiently during onboarding.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Consecutive interpretation in Interpreter agent will be generally available
messageCenterItems.summary: Consecutive interpretation in Microsoft Teams Interpreter, currently in public preview, will roll out to general availability by late 2026. It offers turn-by-turn AI-generated spoken translation using usage-based billing with Copilot Credits. Organizations must set spending policies and have eligible meeting organizers with Copilot licenses.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 16, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

Introduction

Consecutive interpretation in Interpreter for Teams meetings, currently in public preview, is planned to begin rolling out to general availability. This is a new mode in Interpreter that helps meeting participants collaborate more naturally in bilingual conversations. After an eligible meeting organizer turns it on, this turn-by-turn experience interprets each statement after a speaker finishes and then plays the interpreted audio for all meeting participants to hear. 

Similar to other new advanced Microsoft AI experiences, consecutive interpretation will be delivered through usage-based billing (UBB) with Copilot Credits. Usage charges can begin after an administrator configures a spending policy and an eligible meeting organizer turns on the experience for their meeting. A Copilot license is also required as a pre-requisite for the organizer of the meeting. 

The existing simultaneous interpretation mode in Interpreter for Teams meetings and Rooms, which is generally available, hasn't changed. It's still a personal listening experience that includes 20 hours of interpreted audio per month through a Copilot license or a Teams Rooms Pro license. Access beyond the hours included is subject to available capacity, limitations, and additional terms.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 557180.

When this will happen

  • Targeted Release: Rollout begins in early May 2026 (previously early April) and is expected to complete by late May 2026 (previously mid-April).
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in mid-November 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

How this will affect your organization

Who is affected: 

Organizations that use Interpreter in Teams meetings, including public preview users of consecutive interpretation. 

  • In a meeting, an eligible organizer can select More > Interpreter > Consecutive interpretation (uses credits), then choose the two spoken languages. 
  • Consecutive interpretation waits for each speaker to finish, then provides AI-generated spoken interpretation so that all participants hear the same interpreted speech. Interpretation quality may vary depending on audio quality, participant speech patterns, network conditions, and language pair. 
  • Available in Teams meetings on Windows, Mac and web; not currently supported in Teams Events, calls or Teams Rooms.

What you need to do to prepare

  • You will need to set up spending policies to enable consecutive interpretation for eligible meeting organizers. Learn more: Managing AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing | Microsoft Learn 
  • When the experience is generally available, updates will be published to the Copilot Credits Guide so you can review pricing rates and estimate costs for your organization.
  • Learn more
